            BYLAW NO. 1941
            ''Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 606, (790 & 794 Latoria Rd), Bylaw No.
            1941, 2021".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1940 and 1941 at 5:35 pm.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Mark Johnson has applied on behalf of Marlene
Norbury and Michael, Katherine and Nigel Staton to amend the Official Community Plan designation of
790 Latoria Road from Agriculture to Hillside or Shoreline and to amend the zoning of 790 and 794 Latoria
Road from the AGl (Agriculture 1) and RR2 (Rural Residential 2) Zones to the R2 (One- and Two-Family
Residential) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 25 duplex lots.

As part of these application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of these applications, the applicant has agreed to provide the following as a bonus for
increased density per single family equivalent dwelling created:

        a. $660towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund per half duplex or single-family lot less
            than 550 m^;
        b. $3,960towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund per halfduplex or single-family lot less
            than 550 m^;
        c. $1,000 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund per single family lot 550 m^ or greater;
        d. $6,000towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund per single family lot 550 m^ or greater; as
           well as an additional $190,254 as an additional contribution to the General Amenity Reserve
            Fund, and a further contribution of $94,080 towards the General Amenity Reserve fund as
            compensation for the removal of the subject property from the ALR;

The applicant will also agree, through a Section 219 Covenant registered on title priorto Bylaw Adoption,
to provide the following to Bylaw No. 1000 standards and to the satisfaction of the Director of
Engineering:

        •    full frontage improvements;
        •   a construction parking management plan;
        •   a detailed stormwater management plan, and implementation of that plan;

This covenant will also require the owner to:

        •   Construct a multi-use trail along the Latoria Road frontage of the subject properties, and
            complete all associated landscaping and remediation work to the satisfaction of the Parks
            Manager;
        •   Dedicate a 5m wide section of road adjacent to Latoria Road to the satisfaction of the Parks
            Manager;

                                                                                                    February 16, 2021
                                                                                                         Page 3 of 28


        •   Provide a 2.8% cash in lieu of parkland dedication payment at the time of subdivision to the
            satisfaction of the Approving Officer, in accordance with Section 510 of the Local Government
            Act;
        •   Construct a 4.5 m trail connecting the proposed southern cul de sac with Latoria Road and
            register an SRW to the satisfaction of the Parks Manager;
        •   Acknowledge that the site is in proximity to agricultural areas and the South Vancouver Island
            Rangers gun range, and that these uses may create general noise, odour, and other nuisances,
            and agree that the owner and all future owners assume all risk and annoyance of such
            nuisances; and
        •   Obtain a form and character development permit for the entire site prior to subdivision
            approval.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Councilor Sahlstrom - Regarding the unfinished projects by developers in Langford. Wishes to have projects
completed by developers before starting new developments. Complaints from people in City of Langford.
Would like a Moratorium put on Latoria and South Happy Valley Road. Traffic complaints on Latoria Road,
Happy Valley Road, Sooke Road and Jacklin Road. Traffic diverting through other neighborhoods.

L. Plonk. Whimfield Terr - Heartened to hear Councilor Sahlstrom comments. Echoes the issues of traffic.
It's a designated truck route. Piecemeal sidewalks and bike lanes available to residences not completed are
dangerous. Routing traffic instead from Latoria to Deltona to Whimfield Terr or onto Goldspur Ave.
50 homes being built will double traffic to the area. Director of Engineering discussed the width of roadway
and is the standard, but will look into street painting. The standard of single-family homes is 550 m2 and
yet this development is 600 m2 of 2 homes. Lackof greenspace on developments. Taking down of trees and
being deprived of greenspace. Then getting cash in lieu of greenspace. Preserved riparian areas are
unusable. Propose parkland all along top of this development. Take people from Planning dept to Parks
dept to development more greenspace. Another rushed development between PZAH committee and
Council is too rushed. Residents don't feel they are prepared for this change.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

L. Plonk, Whimfield Terr- Letters sent to City of Langford regarding this Bylaw. Stacking positive opinions
to the agenda.

W Hobbs, Luxton Rd - Extreme traffic on Luxton Rd. Really hope the developer has to address concerns of
older neighborhoods No sidewalks and not a legal road.

R. Sanstrom, White Pine Terr-Spoke about the development. Addressing concerns of traffic. Committed
to construction road. Blasting will follow zoning of City.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers. There being none, he declared the Public Hearing
for Bylaw No. 1940 and 1941 closed at 5:54 p.m.

That Council


       1. Proceed with consideration of Bylaw No. 1952 to amend the zoning designation of the
          properties located at 753 and 761 Station Avenue from the C3 (District Commercial) and RM7
          (Medium-Density Apartment) zones to the CCl (City Centre) zone subject to the following
          terms and conditions:


                   a)   That the owner agrees to provide, as a bonus for increased density, the following
                           contributions per dwelling unit, prior to issuance of a Building Permit:
                           i.      $2,850 towards the General Amenity Reserve Fund; and
                           ii.     $750 towards the Affordable Housing Reserve Fund

                   subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable
                   Housing and Amenity Contribution Policy.

                   b)   That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:
                           i.      A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be
                                   adequately managed on-site for the proposed developments, to the
                                   satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

                                                                                               February 16, 2021
                                                                                                    Page 7 of 28


        c)   That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a Section 219 covenant,
             registered in priority of all other charges on title, that agrees:
                i.       That the following will be provided and implemented to Bylaw No. 1000
                standards to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering prior to the issuance of
                a building permit:
                        a.      Full frontage improvements, including 90-degree parking stalls on
                                Aprell Place, if feasible;
                        b.      A storm water management plan; and
                        c.      A construction parking management plan.
                ii.    That 100% of residential parking spaces, excluding visitor parking spaces, shall
                       feature an energized outlet capable of providing Level 2 charging or higher to
                       the parking space, and that
                          a.       Energized outlets shall be labelled for the use of electric vehicle
                                   charging;
                          b.       Where an electric vehicle energy management system is
                                   implemented (load sharing), a qualified professional may specify a
                                   minimum performance standard to ensure a sufficient rate of
                                   electric vehicle charging; and
                          c.       The owner/tenant is required to keep the Electric Vehicle
                                   Servicing Equipment (EVSE) in operation and the Strata
                                   Council/landlord may not prevent an owner, occupant, or tenant
                                   from installing the EV charging equipment
                iii.      That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building
                          permit that prohibits a private or public event, ceremony, function, or the
                          like from occurring in the Banquet Facility and the Legion Hall at the same
                          time, to the satisfaction of the City's Chief Administrative Officer; AND

2. Waive all required amenity contributions for the 65-unit subsidized affordable housing rental
   development proposed with this application subject to the owner registering a section 219
   covenant on title requiring the residential units be subsidized non-profit affordable housing
   units for at least 10-years; AND

3. Replace Section 6.57.08(3) with the following:
   "Surface parking stalls may be located adjacent to an interior side or rear lot line when
   screened by a fence no less than 1.8m (6.0 ft) in height and by a landscaping strip no less than
   1.0m (3.3 ft) in width."; AND

4. Add the following to Appendix J, as section 2.1(g):
   'The Director of Planning may approve development permits with variances to landscaping
   requirements where the design intent of these guidelines and the zone are met"; AND

5. Authorize the Director of Planning it issue the following variances in the Form and Character
   Development Permit for 753 and 761 Station Avenue:
        a)      That Table 1 of Section 4.01.01 be varied to reduce the number of onsite parking
                stalls from the required 214 to 148;
        b)      That Section 6.57.06(l)(b) be varied to reduce the minimum interior side yard
                setback from the required 3.0m to 2.2m;

                                                                                                        February 16, 2021
                                                                                                             Page 8 of 28


                    c)     That Section 6.57.06(2)(a) be varied to reduce the minimum front lot line setback
                           from the required 4.0m to 2.7m.
